description: Punjab Farm Water Watch by The SMAP Squad uses NASA SMAP soil moisture, Landsat, ECOSTRESS & FIRMS fire data to solve Punjab's water crisis and Delhi's air pollution. We turn satellite data into simple Green/Yellow/Red irrigation alerts in Hindi/Punjabi and suggest low-water crops. Our tool saves groundwater, prevents stubble burning, and helps farmers take data-driven decisions.
summary:
Punjab Farm Water Watch is an operational agro-hydrological diagnostic and early-warning web platform built to combat rapid groundwater depletion across Punjab's agricultural belt—a crisis that directly threatens regional harvests and national food security, including Delhi NCR.

By combining NASA SMAP rootzone soil moisture, Landsat 8/9 canopy NDVI/SAVI, NASA GIBS Live, and Black Marble imagery, the platform visualizes district-level water stress through an interactive choropleth dashboard, 7-day moisture outlooks, and AgriSense soil-health diagnostics (pH, EC, and organic carbon balance).

Instead of keeping Earth observation data locked in complex portals, we translate satellite telemetry into immediate, farmer-ready actions—delivering irrigation pause alerts, Direct Seeded Rice (DSR) and mulching recommendations, one-tap WhatsApp and voice advisories in English, Hindi, and Punjabi, and a Panchayat Leaderboard to encourage village-level water conservation.
details:
Project Overview & How It Works

Punjab Farm Water Watch ("From Space to Khet") is an operational agro-hydrological diagnostic and early-warning web platform designed to combat rapid groundwater and rootzone depletion across Punjab. By bridging satellite Earth observation data with field-level decision-making, the platform combines NASA SMAP rootzone soil moisture metrics and Landsat canopy vegetation indices (NDVI/SAVI) into a unified, district-level dashboard.

The application features six interactive modules—Mission & Map, Analytics, 7-Day Outlook, AgriSense, Water Pass, and Leaderboard—allowing users to inspect district choropleth water-stress maps across four selectable basemaps (Dark Matter, Esri Satellite, NASA GIBS Live, and NASA Black Marble). For instance, when telemetry detects high composite water stress (such as Bathinda reaching a Red Risk score of 81.8/100 alongside a drop in SMAP soil moisture), the system automatically generates targeted field advisories.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Punjab’s agricultural productivity—and the broader Delhi NCR food supply—faces severe pressure from unsustainable groundwater extraction. Punjab Farm Water Watch translates complex satellite telemetry into immediate, actionable irrigation guidance for farmers and local panchayats. Recommendations such as pausing irrigation for 3 days to preserve root aeration, adopting Direct Seeded Rice (DSR), and applying crop-residue mulching help conserve groundwater, protect long-term soil health (pH, electrical conductivity, and organic carbon), and reduce unnecessary pumping costs.

Tools, Data & Technologies Used

- Satellite & Earth Observation Data: NASA SMAP (Soil Moisture Active Passive), Landsat (NDVI/SAVI canopy metrics), NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services), and NASA Black Marble.

- Development & Deployment: Built using modern web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript), interactive geospatial mapping layers, and deployed via Netlify (https://punjab-farm-water-watch.netlify.app/).

- Open-Source Repository: https://github.com/arnavskp311-debug/The-SMAP-Squad

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

- Accessibility & Multilingual Support: Recognizing that technical literacy and language barriers often prevent farmers from using scientific tools, we designed the platform with instant switching across English, Hindi, and Punjabi, a Dark Mode interface, 1-tap WhatsApp sharing, and a Listen Voice audio playback feature.

- Community Engagement: Beyond individual field diagnostics, we included a Panchayat Leaderboard and personalized Water Pass to encourage village-level water conservation and track long-term sustainability.
